method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of a person injured in State custody or care, or by a public body, who has a cause of action apart from the Charter, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates in one module, the rules in another, the person's exported questions in a third (each calls a rule in the core), worked cases in a fourth; one regulative rule (s 35, notice to the Attorney-General and the Commission) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006, Act No. 43/2006, Version No. 015 (incorporating amendments as at 1 June 2022), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/charter-of-human-rights-and-responsibilities-act-2006.txt (text sha256 e623948ab9ae63b2aa1fd78cde50280239be3b81eeacee77db480d87ef0ad82e), converted from the Word file saved by hand by the owner on 2026-11-07

seat: the injured person: a person injured in State custody or care, or by a public body (a prisoner, a person held by police, a child in youth justice custody or out-of-home care, a patient detained or restrained under mental health law, a person hurt by a council or State agency), who has or may have a cause of action apart from the Charter (chr-seat.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run chr-dates.l4 ; l4 run chr-core.l4 ; l4 run chr-seat.l4 ; l4 run chr-cases.l4
checks.result: 194 assertions written, 194 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: s 2 (commencements), s 3 (child, person, statutory provision, act), s 4 (public authority, every limb and exclusion), s 6(1), Part 2 (ss 9, 10, 13, 21, 22, 23, 24 limb by limb; every right in ss 8-27 named and reachable through the s 38 question), s 7(2), s 31(2), (6)-(8) (effect and life of an override declaration), s 32, s 35 (the regulative rule), s 36(5), s 38, s 39, s 49(1)-(3). Out: s 1; ss 28-30, s 31(1)-(5), (9), ss 33-34, 36(1)-(4), (6), (7), 37, Part 4, ss 44-46, s 49(4) (machinery of Parliament, the courts, the Attorney-General, the Minister and the Commission); ss 5, 48 (no rule a person applies); the other Part 2 rights limb by limb (named, reachable through s 38); the regulations (not deposited; asked); the other law that gives the claim (asked). Reasons in NOTES.md.
questions: Is the body that hurt me a public authority
Did what happened limit my right to life
Did what happened limit my protection from cruel treatment
Did what happened limit my right to privacy
Did my arrest or detention limit my right to liberty
Were my rights as a person charged limited
Was my right to humane treatment limited
Were my rights as a child in the criminal process limited
Was my right to a fair hearing limited
Was the act unlawful under the Charter
Can I add a Charter ground to my claim
Can I get damages for the Charter breach
Must the court read the statute compatibly with my rights
Must I notify the Attorney-General and the Commission
